So my question is, is Q1'24 the outlier here? Is there anything in Q1'24 which was impacting that year-on-year [comparator] that you want to call out. Secondly, the structural hedge. You change your assumption from 75% to 90%. Your peers are all 100%, in one case even more than 100%, and even seeing some growth in the notional. So any reason why you didn't go to 100%? Why that reticence still?",
  "answer_quote": "So, how do we feel about FICC? I would say a couple of things, the first is we are definitely performing better across a range of products. If I go back to some of the periods that you call out, we would not have had the same kind of Securitised Product business, Trading business that we have. Our European Rates business, as we said, has been an area of focus for us. That was very strong historically, we lost market share. We started of focusing on building that market share back through last year, it was definitely a journey through last year and it performed much better in Q1. The other thing I would call out is Fixed Income Financing within here, equally as part of our Financing businesses, are a much more stable source of revenues and Financing in general is a business that we've invested a lot in. We see good balanced growth and robust margins. So I would say the underlying position is objectively good. In any particular quarter, your [comparators] will either help you or weaken your result, that is just the nature of this business. I would say Q1'24 [was] maybe a little bit weaker, but then if you look at the trajectory and exit rate from 2024 into 2025, I think that would take you back towards this stronger position. From our perspective, what we're really focused on is, are those businesses performing well and in the way we would expect them to, [with] the market share as an output. On the structural hedge, I think Robin touched on this on the day [of results], I'm going to say the same thing again, we said broadly 90% as a planning assumption. We've also said we see stability in margins, we see the hedge being broadly stable. As we saw in Q1, so it's a planning assumption for the maths. What we actually see is probably a bit more stability than that. Dan, what would you add? We're seeing a bit more deposit stability in line with the rest of the UK bank market, so to some extent there will be a market dynamic, rather than Barclays versus peers dynamic.",
